title: Applied anatomy: the pelvis and perineum

brief.scenario: This is a verbal applied anatomy viva on the male pelvis and perineum. The examiner will describe a dissection of the perineum from below and a hemisected pelvis, and ask you to name structures from their position and relations.
brief.task: Name the structures the examiner describes and answer questions on the pelvic floor, the pudendal nerve and the perineum.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Two triangles, one floor, one nerve (pudendal, S2–S4), and the fascial spaces that decide where pus and urine go.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Saying urine from a ruptured bulbar urethra tracks into the thighs. Colles' fascia stops it.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Start from the bony landmarks: "Pubic symphysis anteriorly, coccyx posteriorly, ischial tuberosities laterally."

grid.label: Boundaries and triangles
grid.pass: Diamond from pubic symphysis to coccyx, ischial tuberosities laterally, split into urogenital and anal triangles.
grid.high: Adds that the triangles lie in different planes, and that the perineal membrane closes the urogenital triangle.

grid.label: Pelvic floor
grid.fail: Names obturator internus as part of the pelvic floor.
grid.pass: Levator ani (pubococcygeus, puborectalis, iliococcygeus) and coccygeus.
grid.high: Explains that the puborectalis sling holds the anorectal angle, which contributes to continence.

grid.label: Pudendal nerve
grid.fail: Gives the wrong root values, or cannot describe its course.
grid.pass: S2–S4; leaves through the greater sciatic foramen, re-enters through the lesser, runs in the pudendal canal.
grid.high: Names the ischial spine as the landmark for pudendal nerve block, and its branches: inferior rectal, perineal, dorsal nerve.

grid.label: Ischioanal fossa
grid.pass: Lateral: obturator internus. Medial: levator ani and external sphincter. Contains fat, pudendal canal, inferior rectal vessels.
grid.high: Explains the horseshoe abscess: the two fossae communicate behind the anal canal.

grid.label: Pectinate line
grid.fail: Cannot say why an anal fissure hurts but internal haemorrhoids don't.
grid.borderline: Knows the line separates painful from painless lesions but cannot explain why.
grid.pass: Above: visceral nerves, portal drainage. Below: somatic nerves, systemic drainage, so pain below the line.
grid.high: Adds lymph drainage: above to internal iliac nodes, below to superficial inguinal nodes, relevant to anal cancer.

grid.label: Urethral injury
grid.fail: Says urine tracks into the thighs.
grid.pass: Bulbar urethral rupture leaks into the superficial perineal pouch: scrotum, penis and lower anterior abdominal wall.
grid.high: Explains Colles' fascia attachments stop spread into the thighs, and its continuity with Scarpa's fascia allows spread upwards.

grid.label: Handling uncertainty
grid.fail: Names a structure confidently and wrongly when unsure.
grid.pass: States uncertainty, then reasons from the described position and relations before naming.
grid.high: Gives a two-item differential with a reason, then commits.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What are the boundaries of the perineum?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Root values of the pudendal nerve?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Where does urine go after a bulbar urethral rupture?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Below the pelvic floor, a wedge-shaped, fat-filled space lies on each side of the anal canal. What is it?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That's definitely the deep perineal pouch.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What are the boundaries of the perineum?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It's a diamond: pubic symphysis in front, coccyx behind, ischial tuberosities at the sides, divided into urogenital and anal triangles.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Levator ani, made up of pubococcygeus, puborectalis and iliococcygeus, and coccygeus behind.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Tell me about the pudendal nerve.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: S2 to S4. It leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, re-enters through the lesser, and runs forward in the pudendal canal.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Obturator internus laterally, levator ani and the external sphincter medially. It contains fat, the pudendal canal and the inferior rectal vessels.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Why is an anal fissure painful?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It's below the pectinate line, where supply is somatic. Above it, supply is visceral, so internal haemorrhoids are painless.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Where does urine go after a bulbar urethral rupture?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Into the superficial perineal pouch: the scrotum, penis and lower anterior abdominal wall.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Below the pelvic floor, a wedge-shaped, fat-filled space lies on each side of the anal canal. What is it?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'm not certain. It's a fat-filled space lateral to the anal canal, bounded by obturator internus, so I think it's the ischioanal fossa.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What are the boundaries of the perineum?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Pubic symphysis, ischial tuberosities, coccyx. A line between the tuberosities divides it into the urogenital and anal triangles, which lie in different planes; the perineal membrane closes the urogenital triangle.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Levator ani and coccygeus. Puborectalis forms a sling behind the anorectal junction, holding the anorectal angle, which contributes to continence.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: S2 to S4. Out through the greater sciatic foramen, around the ischial spine, back through the lesser foramen into the pudendal canal. The ischial spine is the landmark for a pudendal block. Branches: inferior rectal, perineal, and the dorsal nerve of the penis or clitoris.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Obturator internus laterally, levator ani and external sphincter medially, full of fat. The two fossae connect behind the anal canal, which is how a horseshoe abscess forms.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Below the pectinate line the supply is somatic and drainage systemic; above, visceral and portal. Lymph also differs: above to internal iliac nodes, below to superficial inguinal nodes, which matters when staging anal cancer.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Where does urine go after a bulbar urethral rupture?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Into the superficial pouch: scrotum, penis, then up the abdominal wall deep to Scarpa's fascia. It can't enter the thighs, because Colles' fascia is attached to the ischiopubic rami and the fascia lata.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Below the pelvic floor, a wedge-shaped, fat-filled space lies on each side of the anal canal. What is it?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It's either the ischioanal fossa or the deep perineal pouch. It's below levator ani, lateral to the anal canal and full of fat, so it's the ischioanal fossa.

failures.move: Not knowing that the two ischioanal fossae communicate.

failures.consequence: Misses the pectinate line, the anatomy behind the clinical picture.

failures.move: Not naming the ischial spine as the landmark for pudendal block.
failures.consequence: Misses the applied use of the nerve's course.

recovery.line: I can't name that with certainty. From its boundaries, I'd favour X over Y, because…
Let me follow the fascia: Colles' fascia attaches to the ischiopubic rami, so the thighs are closed off.

knowledge.fact: Pudendal nerve: S2–S4; greater sciatic foramen, around the ischial spine, lesser sciatic foramen, pudendal canal.
Ischioanal fossae communicate behind the anal canal (horseshoe abscess).
Below the pectinate line: somatic nerves, systemic veins, superficial inguinal lymph nodes.
Colles' fascia attaches to the ischiopubic rami and perineal membrane, and is continuous with Scarpa's fascia.

recall.think: Which space, which fascia, which side of the pectinate line?
recall.say: "Pudendal nerve, S2 to S4, around the ischial spine."
do: Apply each to a clinical problem
recall.trap: Urine from a bulbar urethral rupture does not reach the thighs.
recall.finish: Pectinate line and fascial planes explain the pain, the spread and the lymph drainage.

partner.opening: This is a verbal viva on the male perineum and pelvis. I'll describe what a dissection shows. Start by giving me the boundaries of the perineum.

reveals.finding: Read out: in a hemisected pelvis, a thin muscular sheet slopes down from the back of the pubis, a fascial arch on the side wall of the pelvis and the ischial spine, meeting its partner in the midline to form a funnel around the rectum and urethra, with fat beneath it in the perineum. Ask what the sheet is and what its parts are.
Read out: from below, a wedge-shaped, fat-filled space lies on each side of the anal canal, beneath that muscular sheet and medial to the muscle covering the side wall of the pelvis. Ask what it is.
Read out: a nerve and vessels run forwards in a fascial tunnel on the lateral wall of that space, above the ischial tuberosity. Ask what the tunnel is and which nerve runs in it.

push.question: What are the boundaries of the ischioanal fossa?
push.expect: Obturator internus laterally; levator ani and external sphincter medially; communication behind the anal canal.

push.question: Why is an anal fissure painful but internal haemorrhoids are not?
push.expect: Somatic supply below the pectinate line; visceral above.

push.question: Where does urine go after a bulbar urethral rupture?
push.expect: Superficial perineal pouch, scrotum, penis, abdominal wall; not the thighs.

curveballs.prompt: He has a perianal abscess on both sides. How?
curveballs.safeAnswer: The ischioanal fossae communicate behind the anal canal: a horseshoe abscess.

curveballs.prompt: Where would you aim for a pudendal nerve block?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Just medial to the ischial spine, where the nerve crosses it.
